paragraphs:
R' Abba bar Yehuda — Eruvin ch. 6, halakha 6 [Jerusalem Talmud].
Issi bar Yehuda — Shabbat 6b.
R' Elazar ben Yehuda (a tanna) — Zavim ch. 1, mishna 1.

R' Yosi son of R' Yehuda — Nedarim ch. 8, mishna 6.
Mattityah bar Yehuda — Menachot 79b.
R' Shimon ben Yehuda — Makkot ch. 3, mishna 6.
R' Tanchum bar Yehuda — Berakhot ch. 9, halakha 4 [Jerusalem Talmud].

notes.text: "Jerusalem Talmud" is not printed by Hyman. It is supplied in square brackets because the locator is given by chapter and halakha, which is the Yerushalmi format.

The Hebrew locators are rendered as printed. Colon after a daf number is read as amud b and full stop as amud a; chapter and halakha/mishna numbers are kept as printed. Whether Eruvin, Berakhot ch. 9 and similar references are Yerushalmi or Mishna is inferred from the chapter/halakha format.
This is a list of several different people named after a father Yehuda, not one person; the source is only a name collection with locators.

No new named source was supplied. The empty model findings array does not cancel the root’s seven held units or eight abbreviated-title occurrences. All eleven units and every separate name, full Rav title, unexpanded R-prime title, numeral and inferred bracketed Yerushalmi label remain. Issi and Mattityah have no added titles. The collection is not one person, one father or an admitted genealogy; all locator conventions remain distinct from verified source matches.

This list follows Hyman’s names and locators as supplied. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:6 has R’ Ba bar Yehuda. Shabbat 6b has Issi ben Yehuda, Zavim 1:1 Eliezer ben Yehuda, Menachot 79b Mattityah ben Yehuda, and Shabbat 79a Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda. Hyman’s printed Dostai locator appears as Kiddushin 24a (vol. II, p. 533), while the supplied text has 25a. The consulted Kiddushin 64a and 77a name R’ Dostai ben Yehuda. The consulted Sanhedrin 77b names Rav Chinena bar Yehuda, while Hyman gives 76b. Nedarim 8:6 gives “R’ Yose, his son” after the preceding teaching of R’ Yehuda. The prayer teaching in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:5 has R’ Tanchuma ben Yehuda. Ketubot 21a presents Rav Chiya and Rav Huna among alternative attributions, and the consulted Berakhot 8a and Makkot 3:6 support their respectively named Huna and Shimon notices.
